steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState from 'react' here

// Your component will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Import DatePicker component from 'react-datepicker'
steps.instruction: Import the DatePicker component from the 'react-datepicker' package.
steps.hint: Use a named import to bring DatePicker into your component file.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing a component from a library
import { Button } from 'some-ui-library';
steps.expectedOutcome: The DatePicker component will be available for use in your component.
successCriteria: The import statement for DatePicker from 'react-datepicker' is correctly added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the DatePicker component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing DatePicker from the correct package 'react-datepicker'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import DatePicker from 'react-datepicker'.

steps.title: Import CSS for DatePicker styling
steps.instruction: Import the CSS stylesheet for the DatePicker component from 'react-datepicker/dist/react-datepicker.css'.
steps.hint: Add an import statement for the CSS file to apply the default styling to the DatePicker component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing a CSS file for a component
import 'some-library/dist/some-library.css';
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS import statement is added, enabling the default styling for the DatePicker component.
successCriteria: The code includes an import statement for 'react-datepicker/dist/react-datepicker.css'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the CSS styles for the DatePicker. This will ensure the component has proper styling when rendered.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing the exact path 'react-datepicker/dist/react-datepicker.css'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS import is missing or incorrect. You need to add: import 'react-datepicker/dist/react-datepicker.css';

steps.title: Create the main ControlledDatePicker component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ControlledDatePicker that returns a JSX element. The component should be defined as a function (either using function declaration or arrow function) and return a JSX element like a <div>.
steps.hint: You can use either 'function ControlledDatePicker()' or 'const ControlledDatePicker = () =>'. Make sure to return a JSX element (like a <div>) from the function body.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named ControlledDatePicker is created that returns a JSX element.
successCriteria: The code should contain a function or arrow function named ControlledDatePicker that returns a JSX element (like a <div>).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ControlledDatePicker component. This is the foundation for our controlled date picker.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a function named ControlledDatePicker that returns a JSX element (like a <div>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Please create a function named ControlledDatePicker that returns a JSX element.

steps.title: Initialize selectedDate state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside your ControlledDatePicker component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named selectedDate, initialized to null. Make sure to properly type it as Date | null.
steps.hint: Use useState<Date | null>(null) to create the state variable and its setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a selectedDate state variable that will store the currently selected date value, initialized to null.
successCriteria: The code should include useState<Date | null>(null) inside the component body, creating both selectedDate and setSelectedDate variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the selectedDate state with proper TypeScript typing. This gives us a place to store the date value selected by the user.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include the type annotation <Date | null> for useState and initialize it with null. Also ensure the state declaration is inside the component body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. You need to use useState<Date | null>(null) inside the component to create the selectedDate state variable.

steps.title: Define handleDateChange handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the ControlledDatePicker component, define a function named handleDateChange that takes a parameter of type Date | null and updates the selectedDate state using its setter function.
steps.hint: Create an arrow function or function declaration that accepts a date parameter and calls setSelectedDate with that parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleDateChange function is defined that will be used to update the selectedDate state when the user selects a date.
successCriteria: The function should be named handleDateChange, accept a Date | null parameter, and call setSelectedDate with that parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the handleDateChange function that will update the selectedDate state when called.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function accepts a Date | null parameter and calls setSelectedDate with that parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleDateChange function isn't defined correctly. It should take a Date | null parameter and update the selectedDate state using setSelectedDate.

steps.title: Return a wrapper div for the component
steps.instruction: Inside the ControlledDatePicker component's return statement, add a <div> element that wraps the existing <h2> element. This div will serve as the container for the entire component.
steps.hint: Place the existing <h2> element inside a new <div> element in the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a <div> element that contains the <h2> element, creating a proper container structure.
successCriteria: The return statement should contain a <div> element that wraps the <h2> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added a wrapper div around the heading. This provides a proper container structure for your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the <div> element properly wraps the <h2> element in the return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a <div> element that contains the <h2> element. Check your return statement structure.

steps.title: Add a label for the DatePicker
steps.instruction: Inside the wrapper div, add a <label> element with the text 'Select a date:' before the existing heading.
steps.hint: Add a JSX label element with descriptive text. Place it above the existing <h2> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a descriptive label above the heading, preparing for the DatePicker input.
successCriteria: Add a JSX <label> element with the text 'Select a date:' inside the wrapper div, placed before the existing <h2> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a descriptive label for the DatePicker. This helps users understand what the input is for.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a label, but check the text content or placement. Make sure it says 'Select a date:' and appears before the <h2> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The label wasn't added correctly. Add a <label> element with the text 'Select a date:' inside the wrapper div, above the heading.

steps.title: Add the DatePicker component with selected prop
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement, add the DatePicker component with its selected prop set to the selectedDate state variable.
steps.hint: The DatePicker component accepts a selected prop that controls its displayed date. Pass selectedDate as the value for this prop.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding a DatePicker with selected prop
<DatePicker selected={selectedDate} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The DatePicker component will be added to the UI, but it won't be interactive yet since we haven't wired up the onChange handler.
successCriteria: The DatePicker component should be added to the return statement with the selected prop correctly set to selectedDate.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the DatePicker component and connected it to your selectedDate state via the selected prop.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the DatePicker component, but the selected prop might not be correctly set. Make sure you're passing selectedDate as the value for the selected prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DatePicker component hasn't been added correctly. You need to add <DatePicker selected={selectedDate} /> inside the return statement.

steps.title: Wire onChange prop to handleDateChange
steps.instruction: Add the onChange prop to the DatePicker component and set it to the handleDateChange function you defined earlier.
steps.hint: The DatePicker component accepts an onChange prop that should be connected to your handler function. Use the syntax onChange={handleDateChange}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of wiring an onChange handler to an input
<input type="text" onChange={handleInputChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The DatePicker component will now call your handleDateChange function whenever the user selects a new date.
successCriteria: DatePicker component has an onChange prop
onChange prop is set to handleDateChange
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully connected the DatePicker's change event to your handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the onChange prop is correctly set to handleDateChange.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DatePicker component needs an onChange prop connected to the handleDateChange function.

steps.title: Add placeholder text to DatePicker
steps.instruction: Add a placeholderText prop to the DatePicker component with a descriptive string like 'Select a date'.
steps.hint: The placeholderText prop is a string that appears in the input field when no date is selected.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DatePicker input field will show placeholder text when no date is selected.
successCriteria: The DatePicker component includes a placeholderText prop with a string value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The placeholderText prop is correctly added to the DatePicker component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a prop to the DatePicker, but it should be named placeholderText with a string value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DatePicker component still needs a placeholderText prop with a descriptive string.
